n_start: Gallowmere arrives out of the freezing rain looking like a decision somebody regretted immediately: a leaning stockade, a Warden's tower with a lamp burning at the wrong hour, and a muster yard already crowded with companies who got here first. Dellach counts the competition under his breath and does not like the arithmetic. Nyre reads the notice at the gate twice, which is her way of disagreeing with it. Kettle, who has not said a useful word since the hill came in sight, says nothing at all.
a0_tower: Warden-Marshal Ansel Redd lays the commission out without decoration. The winter tax-iron of the Kar Duhn garrison never came down the road, and neither did the garrison. Sixty crowns for the iron and the pay-ledger both, paid on delivery, and no Warden will set foot past the barrow gate with you. He says the last part before you can ask it.
a0_tower_q: His answer is thin and he knows it. Two relief patrols went up to the barrow gate; the first turned back for reasons the sergeant could not commit to paper, and the second came home nine men short. The vault door, both patrols agreed, was standing open exactly a hand's width, and neither of them could say who had opened it.
a0_haggle: The haggle happens in a cold office with the shutters banging, and Redd has no more coin anywhere in his district. What he has instead is a charter: a stamped writ of salvage that would make the Ninth Sword a name on a Warden's list instead of a hired knife. He will part with it only if you drop the hazard pay entirely.
a0_charter: The writ is stamped, sanded, and entered in the tower book by a clerk who spells your company's name correctly on the second attempt. Dellach says nothing whatsoever and stands a little straighter, while Nyre notes in her own book precisely what the arrangement has cost.
a0_sign: The contract is signed with the Marshal's seal still warm, and then he adds his last condition quietly, as though it were an afterthought. Bring back the pay-ledger even if the iron is beyond you. The ledger is what his own account will be measured against, and he would rather be measured accurately.
a0_guide: The only guide willing to take the moor road is Bram Sull, a fen-runner with a drinker's hands, who wants a full share and swears he has walked the dykes blind in fog. Kettle looks at him the way you look at weather coming in from the west, and does not offer an opinion aloud.
a0_guide_hired: Bram is hired out of the advance and has spent a third of his share before the horses are stabled. Dellach considers him unimpressive and Kettle considers him a liability, so the company is five now, and one of the five is a stranger who talks.
a0_dispatch: The garrison's last dispatch is water-stained and written in a clerk's failing hand: routine counts, routine weather, routine complaints about the oil ration. Then, at the bottom, in the same failing hand and pressed much harder, a line that is not routine in any way. The ninth hand is missing and the door will not hold at eight.
a0_taproom: The Broken Wheel is peat smoke and wet wool and three companies drinking on other people's commissions. A charcoal burner at the end of the bench is telling anyone who will listen about lamps that move across the moor in single file. Over by the fire, one of Corrow's Rooks has begun measuring Dellach for a joke he intends to tell loudly.
a0_rumors: A round bought for the room loosens it considerably. The Kar Duhn garrison paid its own wages nine times over on paper, according to a man who used to cart their flour. A Ledger factor came up from the south twice this autumn, which nobody can explain. And nobody in Gallowmere, at any price, will take a contract past the barrow gate.
a0_lamps: Sober enough to be precise, the charcoal burner is extremely precise. Lamps in a file of nine, always nine, moving along the old dwarf road at the same hour of the night. They stop at the barrow gate and wait there a while, as though somebody inside has to count them in before they are permitted to pass.
a0_lamps_full: The remainder costs two coppers. The lamps have come every ninth night since midsummer, as regular as a tax collector, and his brother followed them once out of curiosity and drink. What came back to the charcoal hut four days later was his brother's coat, folded neatly, with every button cut off.
a0_brawl: Corrow's bravo has decided the Ninth Sword is a joke worth telling at volume, and he is most of the way through the second telling. Dellach's hand is already flat on the table, which is invariably how it begins with him, and the room has gone quiet enough to hear the fire working.
a0_brawl_win: It takes three exchanges. The bravo ends up folded over a bench with his opinion of your company substantially revised, and the room's opinion of the Rooks revised in the other direction. Dellach's knuckles are split to the bone. Nyre binds the hand without one word of comment, which is worse than comment.
a0_brawl_bought: A bought drink, a hard smile, and the bravo backs off describing the whole business as professional courtesy. Dellach believes you spent coin on nothing at all; Kettle believes you bought the only thing in Gallowmere actually worth having, which is one quiet night before the moor.
a0_rest: One night in a real bed above a warm floor, with boots off and the door barred, and the company sleeps like paid soldiers instead of hunted ones. You wake before the bell and can feel the difference in your hands.
a0_yard: The muster yard in the rain: two companies loading out, the Rooks' banner pitched over the only dry ground, and a scatter of loose hands hoping for a fourth-share. One of them is a woman in a salt-stained coat, sitting on a crate, reading the warding sigils off a wagon axle as though they were a bill of lading.
a0_ilsabet: Ilsabet Crane, hedge-thaumaturge, glass and salt and one badly burned sleeve. She reads the wagon's warding aloud, corrects it, and then tells you plainly what nobody in the tower would say: whatever emptied Kar Duhn was let in rather than broken in. The marks on the relief patrol's shields were made from the inside.
a0_ilsabet_full: A full share, agreed with a handshake she does not release until you meet her eye. She owns exactly one crate, and everything in it is written on rather than made of anything, and Kettle helps her carry it up without being asked, which from Kettle is a formal endorsement.
a0_ilsabet_half: Half a share, taken with a shrug that costs you something you cannot price yet. She comes, and she works, and she keeps roughly one hand's worth of what she knows in reserve, which is exactly the arrangement you paid for.
a0_spears: The spear-brothers are Odd and Sten, cheap and cheerful and entirely untested, and they ask about the coin twice and about the moor not once. Dellach hires them regardless, on the reasonable grounds that a shield wall of two men is not a shield wall at all.
w0_rooks: Captain Vasse Corrow of the Rooks is dry under an oiled awning with a cup in her hand, and she offers to buy your commission outright for forty crowns, which she describes as mercy. She has been to the barrow gate herself. She will not say what turned her around, and she does not pretend that nothing did.
w0_rooks_drink: Corrow drinks steadily and talks around the edges of it. Her scout went in at the gate and came out wrong, counting under her breath, in nines. She would not stop counting for anything, food included, and she died of it eleven days later in a Ledger hospice with the count still going.
w0_ledger: The Ledger counting room is warm as a church and considerably quieter, and Factor Halloway keeps the frontier's debts in a hand like engraving. Nyre's order and his are the same order, which is precisely why she does not trust him. He offers hot wine and asks after the company's health as if he already knew the answer.
w0_account: Nyre reads the garrison's pay account aloud in the flat voice she reserves for bad news. The Kar Duhn garrison drew its winter pay nine times in nine years, and every single draw was signed by a different hand. The ninth signature, at the bottom of the final page, is not a name at all but a mark.
w0_kit: Credit against the commission, spent properly: oil, dry powder, two lamps with clean wicks, a new haft for Dellach's poleaxe, and enough salt for Ilsabet to work with. The debt settles in behind the company like a second contract, and this one has interest.
w0_indent: Halloway's better offer is laid out with what appears to be genuine kindness. Forget the iron entirely, bring him the pay-ledger alone, and the Ledger will carry the Ninth Sword's debts for nine years, term for term and hand for hand. He uses the word nine twice while explaining it.
w0_kettle: Kettle is up on the rampart with her back to the moor, lying badly about why she took this particular contract. She was born in the fens directly under that hill, and she has not said the words Kar Duhn once since Gallowmere came into view. She is saying them now only because you asked a second time.
w0_kettle_press: The truth comes out in pieces, none of them comfortable. She went under the hill at eleven years old with her father's crew, who were paid in silence and salt to carry crates down the stair and nothing at all back up. She is the only member of that crew still walking around above ground.
w0_rhyme: The crews had a counting rhyme for the stair, and she recites it without any expression whatsoever, the way you recite something you have deliberately not thought about for twenty years. Nine hands on the iron, nine irons in the door. Eight to hold it shut, and the ninth to keep the score.
w0_betray: The Marshal is informed, and the Marshal is pleased, and a note goes into a Warden ledger about a captain who reports things. Kettle is on the wagon at dawn regardless, and does not look at you for two days. The rest of the company noticed which way you jumped, and has filed it.
a0_gather: The last hour in Gallowmere: the company assembled in the yard with its kit checked twice, the moor going blue-black beyond the stockade, and the rain easing into something merely unpleasant. Everything has been settled except the shape of your leaving, and that has to be settled tonight.
a0_march_light: Out at first light with the bell, light kit and good order, and the stockade gate closing behind the last man in the company. The moor opens ahead of you like a held breath, and for the first mile it is almost possible to enjoy the walk.
a0_march_night: A night march in horizontal rain to steal a day on the Rooks: four miles of it, in the dark, on a track nobody can see. By the time the sky greys the company is wet through to the skin, and the head start has been paid for in the only currency the moor accepts.
a0_supply: The advance sits on the table and there is exactly one morning available in which to spend it. Nyre wants a mule, salt, oil and eighty feet of rope; Dellach wants moor-iron and a warded haft for the poleaxe. One of them is purchasing endurance and the other is purchasing edge, and unfortunately both of them are entirely correct.
a0_supply_mule: A bad-tempered mule named Preacher, four stone of salt, a cask of oil and eighty feet of tarred rope. The company jokes about the mule the whole way out of the gate, and will stop joking about the mule well inside the week.
a0_supply_blade: Moor-iron, bought off a smith who would not meet your eye while he wrapped it: a short heavy blade and a warded haft for Dellach's poleaxe. It is cold in the hand in a way that ordinary iron is not, and worth every coin if even half the stories are true.
a0_muster: The causeway out of Gallowmere ends at the edge of the Barrow Moor, which is the last dry ground anybody will stand on for two days. Three ways go forward from here. There is the drover track along the dykes, the straight line across open moor that saves a day, and the old dwarf road, which goes under the hill's shoulder and comes out where nobody living can tell you.
e_a0_insult: You ride south out of Gallowmere with your pride intact and nothing else whatsoever, and the Rooks' banner goes up over the refused commission before you are clear of the stockade. Dellach says the thing you already know exactly once and then never mentions it again, which is that pride does not winter well.
e_a0_moor_night: Out on the moor after dark behind a drunk with a rushlight, following a taproom story to its source. The file of lamps is considerably closer than it appeared from the window, and when it halts, it halts in order to count. The burner runs immediately. The last thing anybody in the company hears is a number, pronounced carefully, in a voice with no throat behind it.
e_a0_gaol: Steel drawn in a Warden town puts the whole company in the stockade cells before midnight. The commission is struck at dawn and handed to the Rooks in the yard, and Redd's clerk reads the forfeiture out loud through the bars in a level voice while Corrow waits outside, being careful not to smile.
e_a0_sell: Forty crowns, split five ways in a wet yard, and the Rooks ride out with your paper before noon. The company is alive and paid and finished as a company, because the story that gets told in every taproom between here and the Ledger cities is the one where the Ninth Sword sold.
e_a0_indenture: Halloway's ink dries on nine years of the company's labour in the time it takes to read the clause twice, which you do not do. The iron is forgotten, the ledger is promised, and Nyre walks out of the counting room without a word, because she has understood what you signed and you have not.
e_a0_walk: The commission is sold on cheap and the road south is taken before the weather turns for good. The moor keeps its garrison and its iron and its arithmetic. The question of what happened under that hill follows the company down every road it takes afterwards, and it is patient, and it never quite closes.
